decisions.reason: A multi-model safety shoe line sits at the firm's core business and involved substantial tooling and development investment, so one year of modest visibility is no reason to write it off.
A low-investment comfort insole with little public commitment would be easy to drop, but it complements the shoe range cheaply and only one year has passed.
The supportive insole overlaps with the other insoles and carries little sunk cost, making it a plausible candidate for consolidation, though early weak results can still be read as temporary.
The ergonomic series has its own page and fits the announced innovation direction, so dropping it would expose a visible commitment and write off considerable investment.
Firefighter boots require costly certification and specialised development, so the sunk costs and long procurement cycles favour persisting despite slow early uptake.
The moulded insole is the home-page flagship central to the firm's stated direction, so abandoning it would publicly contradict management's own choice.
